title: Relationships: ups and downs
subtitle: staunch ally, two-faced, a rift, ups and downs
summary: Describe relationships that work and relationships that break down - loyalty and staunch allies at one end, rifts, feuds and sworn enemies at the other.

lesson.heading: What friendship means
lesson.text: Friends are much more than mere **casual acquaintances** - people you know, but not very well. We expect **loyalty** from our friends, that is support in good or bad times, and we should never speak ill of them **behind their backs**, when they are not there.

examples.text: I've made several **casual acquaintances** since moving to London, but no close friends yet.
A true friend would never talk **behind your back**.
As well as friends, we have relationships with colleagues, **allies** and **partners**.

lesson.heading: Qualities of friendship and their opposites
People on your side and against you
lesson.text: **Allies** are countries or people who join together to fight for a common cause, and your **staunchest ally** is the one you can always rely on. **Business partners** own a business together, but **bitter** or **arch rivals** compete in a negative, aggressive way, and **sworn enemies** will always hate each other.

examples.text: Russia and America were **allies** in the war.
Monica has always been my **staunchest ally** at work. I can always rely on her to support me.
We were business **partners** but now we're **bitter rivals**. Indeed, I could say we are now **sworn enemies**.
Tom and Amy were **arch rivals** at work, but seemed to get on well outside the office.

lesson.heading: Behaving badly
lesson.text: Someone **two-faced** is insincere - pleasant with you and then unpleasant about you behind your back. Someone **distant** is not friendly and rather cold. Note the prepositions: **disloyal to** someone, **dishonest with** someone, **critical of** someone, **two-faced towards** someone.

examples.text: I used to think of Kate as a friend but I now realise she has been **two-faced towards** me.
Fergus has been **disloyal to** me on a number of occasions.
OK, I was **dishonest with** you. I'm sorry, but I didn't want to hurt you.
Sam has been very **distant towards** me recently.
I was amazed that someone who called herself my friend could be so deeply **critical of** me.

lesson.heading: Adverbs and adjectives that strengthen these words
rows: completely and carefully honest in every detail
loyalty that never changes or weakens
a friend who stays with you when others drift away

lesson.heading: When relationships break down
lesson.text: Relationships **break down** (collapse), often because of genuine **misunderstandings**. A **rift** is a serious disagreement that divides people, and **discord** is disagreement and discontent. If you do not **see eye to eye** with someone, you have different opinions; if you are **on bad terms**, you have a poor relationship.

examples.text: Our relationship **broke down** because we were untruthful to each other.
Harry thought I was picking him up and I thought he was getting a taxi. It was a genuine **misunderstanding**.
A serious **rift** has developed between the two union leaders.
My father and I don't **see eye to eye** on most things.
I hate being **on bad terms with** people.

lesson.heading: Expressions for troubled relationships
rows: have good times and bad times
up and down like a car on a bumpy road
a family split up by divorce
a quarrel in a family causing bad feeling for many years

lesson.text: Watch the prepositions: dishonest with someone, critical of someone, disloyal to someone, two-faced towards someone, on bad terms with someone.

exercises.prompt: Match each adjective with its opposite.
We both own the company: we're business ___.
exercises.explanation: Business partners own a business together; rivals compete with each other.

exercises.prompt: Were Britain and the USA ___ in the First World War?
exercises.explanation: Allies are countries or people who join together to fight for a common cause.

exercises.prompt: His ___ honesty is a quality I greatly admire - he is honest in every last detail.
exercises.explanation: Scrupulous honesty is careful, complete honesty; the adverb is scrupulously honest.

exercises.prompt: I don't know why she was so ___ critical of him; it seemed very unfair.
exercises.explanation: Deeply critical is a strong collocation meaning very critical indeed.

exercises.prompt: Her ___ loyalty to him was a mistake. He betrayed her in the end.
exercises.explanation: Unswerving loyalty never changes or weakens.

exercises.prompt: When all my other so-called friends drifted away, Jack always remained a ___ friend to me.
exercises.explanation: A true friend is always there when you need them.

exercises.prompt: I know I'm not perfect, but I've never been dishonest ___ you.
Why are you always so disloyal ___ me?
I realise that people can often be two-faced ___ their boss.
exercises.explanation: You are two-faced towards someone - pleasant to their face, unpleasant behind their back.

exercises.prompt: The kids have been unhappy since their parents divorced. They come from a ___.
exercises.explanation: A broken home is a family split up by divorce.

exercises.prompt: Two of the brothers have not spoken to their other brother for 20 years. I think it's a family ___.
exercises.explanation: A family feud is a quarrel in a family causing bad feeling for many years.

exercises.prompt: Mia and her sister didn't ___ on a lot of things.
exercises.explanation: Not to see eye to eye with someone is to have different opinions from them.

exercises.prompt: Carla's affection for Andrew has ___ lately. I expect they'll split up.
exercises.explanation: If a relationship turns sour, it becomes bad.

exercises.prompt: Henry's brothers are ___ - they will always hate each other.
exercises.explanation: Sworn enemies are people who will always hate each other.

exercises.prompt: Her marriage has been both good and bad at different times. It has had its ___.
exercises.explanation: To have its ups and downs means to have had good and bad times.

exercises.statement: There's been a lot of discord in the office lately means there has been disagreement and discontent.
exercises.explanation: Correct - discord is disagreement and discontent.

exercises.statement: If two people are on bad terms, they have an excellent relationship.
exercises.explanation: To be on bad terms is to have a poor relationship: Jack and his sister have been on bad terms for a long time.

exercises.prompt: Does each word or phrase describe a good relationship or a bad one?
Put this sentence about a broken relationship in order.
exercises.answer: A serious rift has developed between the two union leaders
exercises.explanation: A rift is a serious disagreement that divides people or groups.
